about: Put on a request entity by esv::ServerSoundSystem (bg3.exe+0x2D92180 drains the system's queue of ls::Variant<ServerSoundSystem::PlayRequest, PlayHUDRequest>, 0x18-byte elements with the index at +0x10) and consumed by ServerSoundSystem::ProcessServerSoundRequests (EoCServer.dll+0x4CA630), which forwards it to clients (eoc::notification::PlayServerSoundComponent). macOS: ServerSoundSystem::RequestPlaySound(EntityHandle const&, FixedString const&, bool) / RequestPlayHUDSound. Seen.py context: born at the first shove/throw step together with drop/thrown/steering types; very common afterwards (up to 787 holders).

evidence.says: Both writers bg3.exe+0x2D922B0 (PlayRequest) and bg3.exe+0x2D924B0 (PlayHUDRequest) copy the request's EntityHandle (+0) after checking IsEntityAlive. Live: entity handles.

Writers copy the request FixedString at +8 with IncRef; ProcessServerSoundRequests destroys a FixedString at +8. RequestPlaySound(entity, FixedString, bool): the sound event name. Live: FixedString indices.

PlayRequest writer stores the 0..3 result of a virtual call on the system's sound helper (rejects 2 and >=4); PlayHUDRequest writer stores constant 2. Live: 0..2. Enum name not established (an ESoundObjectType-like value, 4 bytes).

esv::ServerSoundSystem queues PlayRequest {Entity +0, FixedString +8, u8 +0xC, u8 +0xD} (variant tag 0) and PlayHUDRequest {Entity, FixedString, u8 +0xC} (tag 1). The exported request functions differ only in that byte: RequestPlaySound (EoCServer.dll+0x4CA960) and RequestPlayHUDSound (+0x4CA760) write 0 at +0xC, RequestPlaySoundFromResource (+0x4CAA70) and RequestPlayHUDSoundFromResource (+0x4CA860) write 1. Both component writers copy request +0xC here; EoCServer.dll+0x845C60 carries it into PlayServerSoundNotificationRequest +0x10 and bg3.exe+0x2DEE710 stores it at eoc::notification::PlayServerSoundComponent +0x18, which makes the client resolve the sound through the sound bank.

esv::ServerSoundSystem queues PlayRequest {Entity +0, FixedString +8, u8 +0xC, u8 +0xD} (variant tag 0) and PlayHUDRequest {Entity, FixedString, u8 +0xC} (tag 1). This byte is RequestPlaySound's bool (EoCServer.dll+0x4CA960 stores param_3 at request +0xD; the PlayHUDRequest writer stores 1). EoCServer.dll+0x845C60 copies component +0x11 into the notification request +0x11, and bg3.exe+0x2DEE710 stores it at eoc::notification::PlayServerSoundComponent +0x19 (LocalPlayerOnly: the client plays it through PlayerManager::PlaySoundForLocalPlayer); the same function branches on it to pick the receiving peers.
Never written by the creators; live bytes here are uninitialised garbage.
